The Sotogrande Polo Final 2035 is the highlight of the summer season on the Costa del Sol. Whether you're a seasoned polo fan or simply looking for a glamorous day out, arriving by boat from Marbella adds an unforgettable edge. This guide covers everything you need to know about a Marbella boat rental for the Sotogrande Polo Final 2035, from which yacht to choose to what's included in your charter.

Why charter a boat from Marbella for the polo final?

The Santa María Polo Club in Sotogrande is just 20 nautical miles south of Puerto Banús. A boat charter turns the journey into a party: cruise past the Golden Mile, spot La Concha mountain, and anchor near the club for a front-row view of the action. No traffic jams, no parking stress — just sun, sea, and champagne. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, so you can step aboard and be at the polo fields in under 30 minutes.

Sample itinerary: Marbella to Sotogrande Polo Final

  • 10:30 — Board your yacht at Puerto Banús. Meet your skipper and enjoy a welcome glass of cava.
  • 11:00 — Depart south. Cruise past Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and the dunes of Artola.
  • 11:30 — Arrive at Sotogrande Marina or anchor near the polo club (weather permitting).

Pricing and booking tips

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are the best value: €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours — all inclusive. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 variants) start at €4,719 for 4 hours, with a free jet ski. For other yachts, pricing is on request via WhatsApp. We recommend booking at least 4–6 weeks before the polo final, as demand peaks. A 50% deposit secures your date, with the balance due 7 days before departure.

What to bring and wear

Dress smart-casual: linen, sundresses, or polo shirts. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the sea breeze. Swimwear is optional but handy if you plan to anchor for a dip. You can bring your own food and extra drinks — our boats have coolers and ice. Don't forget your camera for the coastline and the polo action.
